posts.text: Very well, it's arguably still chimera-vocal-synth week, so I can fix that. The cat voice sim joins a quartet and instruments that get their sound from physical models.
alt: A quartet of chimera-vocal-synth voices, plus a physically simulated feline voice, sing "Poor Wayfaring Stranger," accompanied by physically simulated guitar and fiddle.

posts.author: yonderdavid.bsky.social
posts.text: The articulation needed a couple repairs: nonzero airflow on the J and an exaggerated release on the D. I called the other sounds good enough. The meow and yowl took some work and iteration against reference recordings. The original yowl sounded like a kazoo.
posts.why: Answer 2, spoken with its card up. The last two sentences are spoken and shown; the cut at the start is marked.

posts.author: yonderdavid.bsky.social
posts.text: My original idea was that the seal synth would hum bass for Greenfields, but it turns out that's still under copyright and covers aren't fair use. And the cat was missing, so the new plan was an older melancholic folk song with caterwauling. The lead singer would end by expressing anger at the cat.

posts.text: The plan was a quartet of male voices (the female synth voices need repair; see the soprano line in the Kyrie). I think the harmony helped fill out the voice a bit and the instruments sounding almost lifelike (the bowing should reverse on long notes) helped make the overall vibe ungoofy.
